exact_math.background: Eight tokens forming the computational basis, sum of projectors I; one signal token aligned to the assigned label projector.
exact_math.utilities: Common signed signal utility, zero on background; full40 logits, zero class biases. Abstract fixture only.
exact_math.assignment_conclusion: Under the aligned-signal/isotropic-background/common-utility assumptions, every label assignment has the same CE. The proof uses the exact row multiset, not only the two checked permutations.
exact_math.important_limit: Does not prove invariance when queries are relabelled but physical inputs/encoder remain fixed; does not rule out training or label-dependent noise effects.
exact_math.geometry_alone_not_utility: Positive, zero and negative common signed readouts give benefit, null and harm versus uniform attention in this abstract fixture.

conditional_proof:
Let40 rank1 queries be five MUBs of8 states in C8. Choose one class y; its signal projector equals its assigned query P_pi(y). Eight background states sum to I. q_r=Tr(P_pi(r)P_pi(y)); alpha_r=(q_r+eps)/(q_r+1+9eps). Every row has q=1 once,0 seven times,1/8 thirty-two times. With all40 signed utilities equal to a on the signal and0 on background and classbias0, CE=log(1+7exp(a(alpha0-alpha1))+32exp(a(alpha1/8-alpha1))). Thus ALL bijective label assignments tie under THESE aligned-signal assumptions, for every a. Changing a's sign preserves query geometry but reverses attention utility versus uniform, and a0 gives log40. This does NOT say relabelling queries with a fixed physical encoder has invariant loss. The aligned-signal distribution changes with the label assignment. It also says nothing about actual optimization or label-dependent noise.
Robust conditional variant: n backgrounds with B=n/8>kappa>=0; ||sumrho_bg-BI||op<=kappa; signal trace distance from its assigned projector<=delta<1. Utilities u_rt=u0+a*1_signal+e_rt, a>0, |e_rt|<=eta; classbias differences c_y-c_r>=-beta. Let T=n+1, L=(1-delta+eps)/(1-delta+B+kappa+T*eps), U(mu)=(min(1,mu+delta)+eps)/(min(1,mu+delta)+B-kappa+T*eps). Measurement duality and monotonicity give margin_y,r>=a(L-U(mu_y,r))-2eta-beta. Hence full40CE<=log(1+7exp(-m(0))+32exp(-m(1/8))) for uniform nuisance bounds. This bound ALSO cannot rank the assignments. Elementary conditional calculation, not novel theory or measured task premise.

independent_static_review.scope_verdict: Pass on mathematical inspection, assuming nonnegative smoothing epsilon and trace distance defined as half the trace norm. The GF(8) trace forms, Pauli phases and projector normalization are consistent: the code represents projectors as numerators divided by 8, so overlap traces are divided by 64. The five bases yield row counts 1, 7 and 32 at overlaps 1, 0 and 1/8. Both full-40 CE formulas are correct under their stated assumptions; the robust margin also correctly includes the normalized-utility error penalty 2 eta and bias penalty beta. Assignment equality applies to the ideal aligned-signal fixture; the robust result supplies an assignment-independent bound, not equality of actual noisy losses. Neither establishes fixed-encoder relabelling invariance or empirical failure. Signed utility can reverse the benefit without changing geometry. Code execution, hashes and source contents were not independently verified here. The supplied bounded source findings and this conditional calculation do not establish a new L5 attention contribution or an exhaustive literature exclusion.
